q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of HDPE tarpaulin?
title: Tarpaulin carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the polymer by weight from your resin supplier, then the plant's electricity for tape extrusion, weaving and lamination. Divide plant energy by kg of tarpaulin passed and add the resin, masterbatch and eyelets for the full figure.

ul: HDPE and LDPE resin by weight; polymer is usually most of the total.
Aluminium or plastic eyelets and rope.
Tape extrusion line, the largest electricity user.
Circular or flat looms for the woven base.
Lamination and coating extruder, then cutting and stitching.

p: Report per kg, and per square metre at a stated GSM for buyers who order by size.

example.title: Worked example: tarpaulin plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 177,500 / 300,000 = 0.592 kg CO2 per kg
Add HDPE resin, masterbatch and eyelets for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
